title: Naturality of the canonical Cech-to-cohomology comparison map
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal U:X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an open covering, viewed as a covering of the Zariski site of $X$ [def-sc-zariski-site]; write $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,-)$ and $\check H^p(\mathcal U,-)$ for its Cech complex and Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $p\geq0$, the *canonical comparison map* $c_{\mathcal F}:\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is defined as follows. Choose an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], and let $T_{\mathcal F}$ be the total complex [def-sp-double-complex-total] of the first-quadrant double complex with terms $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)$. The restriction maps $\mathcal I^q(X)\to\check{\mathcal C}^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)$ give a cochain map $\alpha_{\mathcal F}:\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to T_{\mathcal F}$ and $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^0$ gives a cochain map $\beta_{\mathcal F}:\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to T_{\mathcal F}$. Then $\alpha_{\mathcal F}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $c_{\mathcal F}=H^p(\alpha_{\mathcal F})^{-1}\circ H^p(\beta_{\mathcal F})$, followed by the identification $H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^p(X,\mathcal F)$, does not depend on the choice of the resolution. These maps are natural in $\mathcal F$: for every morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and every $p\geq0$, $c_{\mathcal F'}\circ\check H^p(\mathcal U,\varphi)=H^p(X,\varphi)\circ c_{\mathcal F}$, where $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\varphi)$ is induced by the cochain map $(c_{i_0\dots i_p})\mapsto(\varphi(c_{i_0\dots i_p}))$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma Tag 01EQ (cohomology-lemma-cech-cohomology) and its proof: the transformation of functors $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,-)\to R\Gamma(U,-)$ on Mod(O_X) built from the double complex $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^\bullet)$

proof.text: Fix an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$, which exists by the enough-injectives statement. Form the first-quadrant double complex $D^{p,q}=\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)$ and its total complex $T_{\mathcal F}$. Restriction of global sections gives a cochain map $\alpha_{\mathcal F}:\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to T_{\mathcal F}$ in Cech degree zero, while the augmentation gives $\beta_{\mathcal F}:\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to T_{\mathcal F}$ in resolution degree zero; the Cech functoriality statement supplies the induced cochain maps and their maps on cohomology.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma Tag 01EQ, proof: construction of the double complex and the maps alpha and beta

proof.text: For every injective term $\mathcal I^q$ of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)=0$ for $p>0$ by the injective Cech-acyclicity statement, and $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)=\ker d^0$ is identified with $\mathcal I^q(X)$ by restriction, by the gluing and uniqueness axioms of the sheaf $\mathcal I^q$ on $X_{\rm Zar}$. Regard $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ as the first-quadrant double complex $D'$ concentrated in the column $p=0$ ($D'^{0,q}=\mathcal I^q(X)$, $d_I=0$); since $d^0$ of the restriction of a global section is $0$, $\alpha_{\mathcal F}$ is the map on total complexes of a morphism of double complexes $D'\to D$. By functoriality of the second spectral sequence (rows first, ${}''E_1^{q,p}=H^p_I(D^{\bullet,q})$), this morphism induces on ${}''E_1$ the maps $H^p_I(D'^{\bullet,q})\to\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)$, which are isomorphisms for all $p,q$ by the two facts above; hence it is an isomorphism on ${}''E_\infty$, i.e. on all graded pieces of the finite image filtrations of $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D')=H^n(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ and $H^n(T_{\mathcal F})$ given by convergence, and an induction on the filtration degree with the five lemma shows that $H^n(\alpha_{\mathcal F})$ is an isomorphism for every $n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma Tag 01EQ, proof; Lemma Tag 01EP for injective Cech acyclicity

proof.text: Let $\iota_{\mathcal I}^p:H^p(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ be the isomorphism of the derived-map statement for $v=\Gamma(X,-)$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, which has enough injectives, $H^p(X,-)$ being its right derived functors. Define $c_{\mathcal F}=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}\circ H^p(\alpha_{\mathcal F})^{-1}\circ H^p(\beta_{\mathcal F})$. Independence of the resolution: for a second resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ (with primes for its data), the lift statement gives a morphism of complexes $\psi:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ lifting $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$; by the computation of Step 4 applied to $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$ and the lift $\psi$, the map $\tau$ of total complexes induced by $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\psi)$ satisfies $\tau\alpha_{\mathcal F}=\alpha'_{\mathcal F}\Gamma(X,\psi)$ and $\tau\beta_{\mathcal F}=\beta'_{\mathcal F}$, so $H^p(\alpha'_{\mathcal F})^{-1}H^p(\beta'_{\mathcal F})=H^p(\Gamma(X,\psi))\,H^p(\alpha_{\mathcal F})^{-1}H^p(\beta_{\mathcal F})$, and the derived-map statement with $h=\mathrm{id}$ gives $(\iota^p_{\mathcal J})^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(X,\psi))\iota^p_{\mathcal I}=H^p(X,\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. Hence both resolutions give the same $c_{\mathcal F}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma Tag 01EQ, proof: final derived-category paragraph and independence of the injective resolution

proof.text: For a morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, choose injective resolutions and a lift $\widetilde\varphi:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ with $\widetilde\varphi^0\circ r=r'\circ\varphi$. Applying the Cech functor termwise gives a morphism of double complexes and hence a map of total complexes. The squares with the two alpha maps commute because restriction maps commute with each component $\widetilde\varphi^q$, and the squares with the beta maps commute by the lifting equation in degree zero. Taking cohomology, using the definition of $c_{\mathcal F}$ and the lifted-complex formula for $H^p(X,\varphi)$, yields $c_{\mathcal F'}\circ\check H^p(\mathcal U,\varphi)=H^p(X,\varphi)\circ c_{\mathcal F}$.
